snapshots.name: Victor
snapshots.subtitle: A young Genevan natural philosopher
snapshots.body: The narrator of the central story, obsessed since boyhood with the secrets of life and death. He leaves his family in Geneva to study at Ingolstadt, where his research takes a direction he will not fully explain even to the friend he is writing to.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: the creature
snapshots.subtitle: The being Victor makes
snapshots.body: Assembled by Victor from collected remains and given life in his workshop. He is abandoned by his creator within moments of opening his eyes, before either of them has any idea what he is capable of.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Walton
snapshots.subtitle: An English captain bound for the North Pole
snapshots.body: Writing letters home to his sister as his ship pushes into arctic ice, he pulls a half-frozen stranger aboard and becomes the outer frame through which the whole account reaches the reader. His own hunger for glory mirrors the story he is about to hear.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Mrs. Saville
snapshots.subtitle: Walton's sister in England
snapshots.body: The unseen addressee of Walton's letters, which open and close the novel. She never appears directly; everything the reader learns of her comes through her brother's writing.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: M. Frankenstein
snapshots.subtitle: Victor's father
snapshots.body: A respected Genevan syndic who raised his children with affection and encouraged Victor's education without grasping where his son's private studies were leading. He writes to Victor with family news and worry when letters from home stop coming.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Caroline Beaufort
snapshots.subtitle: Victor's mother
snapshots.body: Daughter of a ruined friend of Alphonse's, taken in and later married by him after her father's death. Her own death, from scarlet fever caught nursing Elizabeth, falls on Victor just before he leaves for university.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Elizabeth Lavenza
snapshots.subtitle: An orphan raised as Victor's cousin and intended bride
snapshots.body: Brought into the Frankenstein household as a small child and raised alongside Victor, who from early on regards her as more than a sister. She stays close to the family through every absence and misfortune that follows.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Henry Clerval
snapshots.subtitle: Victor's closest friend from childhood
snapshots.body: A merchant's son with a taste for poetry and adventure rather than the family business, he follows Victor to Ingolstadt and nurses him through a long illness there. His warmth is a steady contrast to Victor's growing secrecy.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: little William
snapshots.subtitle: Victor's youngest brother
snapshots.body: A cherished child in the Frankenstein family, still young enough to be spoiled by everyone around him. News concerning him is what finally calls Victor back home from his travels with Clerval.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Justine Moritz
snapshots.subtitle: A servant raised almost as a member of the family
snapshots.body: Taken in by Caroline Frankenstein as a girl after trouble at her own home, she becomes devoted to the family, especially to William. She returns to Geneva to visit her mother on the night William goes missing.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Ernest
snapshots.subtitle: Victor's middle brother
snapshots.body: The second Frankenstein son, mentioned in family letters as being intended for a soldier's career against his father's preference for the law. He remains in Geneva through the family's troubles.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: the old man
snapshots.subtitle: A blind old man living in exile in a cottage
snapshots.body: Once a comfortable Parisian, now reduced to a simple rural cottage with his two children, supported by a son's labor and a daughter's care. His blindness makes him the one person the creature can approach without being fled from on sight.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Felix
snapshots.subtitle: De Lacey's son
snapshots.body: A young man carrying his family's poverty and a private grief the creature slowly pieces together by watching the cottage. He works the land and teaches his father's household through hardships that once knew better days.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Agatha
snapshots.subtitle: De Lacey's daughter
snapshots.body: Felix's sister, who shares the daily work and quiet sorrow of the cottage. Her gentleness toward her blind father is part of what teaches the creature what a family can be.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Safie
snapshots.subtitle: An Arabian woman who joins the De Lacey household
snapshots.body: The daughter of a Turkish merchant, she arrives at the cottage seeking Felix, to whom she is devoted, and stays to learn the family's language. Her lessons, overheard by the creature in hiding, become his own education in speech and history.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: M. Krempe
snapshots.subtitle: A professor of natural philosophy at Ingolstadt
snapshots.body: A blunt, unimpressive-looking professor who dismisses Victor's early reading in old alchemical writers as useless. His scorn stings Victor without turning him from science itself.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: M. Waldman
snapshots.subtitle: A professor of chemistry at Ingolstadt
snapshots.body: Kind where Krempe was dismissive, he reframes the old alchemists as flawed pioneers of real modern science and encourages Victor's fascination rather than mocking it. His lectures are what finally set Victor's private research in motion.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.
